result.rationale:
TopicEmbed.import appends `contents << "\n
\n#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")}"` with no HTML escaping of url, which is only validated by `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. Posts created via PostCreator use `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook returns `raw` unmodified for that method, so the injected attribute is rendered via `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb. A crafted feed link containing a quote would break out of the href attribute — stored XSS mechanism verified in the diff.

judged_text: The imported_from footer interpolates url directly into an HTML attribute (`<a href='#{url}'>`) inside raw-HTML-cooked content with no escaping, and url is only regex-checked (`^https?://`), never attribute-escaped. A feed item link like http://x.com/'onmouseover='alert(1) (quotes and equals signs are legal URI path characters, so the embed_url path passes URI parsing too) breaks out of the href attribute, yielding stored attribute-injection XSS rendered raw in the embed and topic view — unsanitized even when the article body went through the readability whitelist.

A feed item link like http://x.com/'onmouseover='alert(1) (quotes and equals signs are legal URI path characters, so the embed_url path passes URI parsing too) breaks out of the href attribute, yielding stored attribute-injection XSS rendered raw in the embed and topic view — unsanitized even when the article body went through the readability whitelist.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the footer is built with `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")` and appended to `contents`. The only validation on `url` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other characters that can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute. Posts created for imports set `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `:raw_html`, bypassing sanitization; the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`. Therefore a crafted feed URL like `http://x.com/'onmouseover='alert(1)` can lead to stored attribute-injection XSS.
